title: Count the Number of Beautiful Subarrays
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, count the number of beautiful subarrays.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, count the number of beautiful subarrays. A subarray is considered beautiful if, through any number of operations, all its elements can be reduced to zero. In each operation, you can choose two different indices i and j (where 0 <= i, j < nums.length), and a non-negative integer k such that the k-th bit (0-indexed) in the binary representation of nums[i] and nums[j] is 1. You then subtract 2^k from both nums[i] and nums[j]. Note that subarrays consisting entirely of zeros are also considered beautiful.
constraints: An operation clears the same set bit from two different elements.
A subarray is beautiful exactly when every bit occurs an even number of times across its elements.
Return the number of beautiful contiguous subarrays.
hints: Clearing equal bits in pairs is possible exactly when every bit count is even.
That condition is equivalent to the subarray XOR being zero.
A subarray XOR is zero when the XOR prefixes at its two boundaries are equal.
Count prior occurrences of each running XOR; each match contributes one distinct beautiful subarray.
editorial: Count prior occurrences of each running XOR; each match contributes one distinct beautiful subarray.

tests.explanation: Exactly two subarrays have XOR zero and therefore even parity at every bit.
Both one-element zero subarrays and the full subarray are beautiful, giving three.
